summary: Under channelBinding=require, fail the SCRAM handshake when no tls-server-end-point hash can be derived from the server certificate or the negotiated mechanism is not -PLUS, instead of silently downgrading (GHSA-j92g-9f8w-j867).

tests.evidence: Security fix; the new mockito test covers the Ed25519 empty-hash path, but the authoritative post-negotiation isPlus() check has no test (codecov: 18% patch coverage, 9 lines missed) and the second test covers pre-existing no-SSL behavior.

user_docs.evidence: use.md/README already define require as 'must employ channel binding'; the fix makes code match docs, though the Ed25519 limitation could be noted.

doc_comments.evidence: Inline comments explain the RFC 5929 gap and the fail-closed intent accurately.

change_description.evidence: Security fix with a user-visible effect ships with no CHANGELOG.md entry (added later in #4270); the PR body explains why and how well.

performance.evidence: Auth handshake only, one extra check.

security.evidence: Changes the channel-binding enforcement in SCRAM authentication (downgrade prevention); a focused security review is mandated. The isPlus() check also closes the remaining empty-array fall-throughs (null or non-X509 peer certificate).

backward_compat.evidence: Connections with channelBinding=require against Ed25519-signed server certificates now fail; intended, since they were silently unprotected.

error_model.evidence: Two new CONNECTION_REJECTED PSQLExceptions with messages naming the signature algorithm or mechanism and the remediation; mandated check, messages look right.

correctness.evidence: Non-trivial control flow in getChannelBindingData and initializeScramClient where a missed branch reopens the downgrade; the belt-and-braces isPlus() check covers the paths that still return an empty array.

user_value.evidence: Security fix, no new feature or option.

surprising_behavior.evidence: require now fails for certificates it previously accepted; the message says why, so not astonishing.

build_ci.evidence: Deliberately keeps scram-client 3.2; no dependency change.

observability.evidence: Failure surfaces as an exception with the algorithm name; the FINEST mechanism log stays; nothing swallowed.

spec_conformance.evidence: Interprets RFC 5929 tls-server-end-point (no hash for Ed25519) and SCRAM -PLUS channel-binding semantics; the interpretation is correct.

plan.why: Small two-file security fix; one security-focused reviewer can cover the auth path, its spec basis, error messages, and test gaps together.
